title: Breathing Techniques for Calm: 5 Patterns, Each in 60 Seconds

copy.cover_headline: Your jaw is tight. Here's a 60-second reset.

points.headline: Start with one body signal
points.body: A tight jaw, raised shoulders, a held breath. Notice just one. Mid-scroll is often when the tension shows up, so it's a useful moment to reset.

points.headline: Two physiological sighs (about 20 s)
points.body: Inhale through your nose, add a short top-up sip, then exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 to 8 seconds. Fill to about three quarters, not to bursting.

points.headline: Then 4-6: in for 4, out for 6
points.body: Inhale gently through your nose for 4, exhale for 6 without forcing. Each breath takes 10 seconds, so 6 breaths fill a minute. Straining? Try 3-5 instead.

points.headline: Check your body, not your watch
points.body: Look for a longer, easier exhale, lower shoulders, a looser jaw. Still wired? Do two more minutes. Dizzy or tingly? Stop and breathe normally.

points.headline: Slow breathing has the best support
points.body: Breathing near 6 breaths a minute has the strongest research behind it. The effect is modest: it can help you feel calmer, but it doesn't switch stress off.

reel_lines: Your jaw sets while your thumb keeps moving.
Then your breath goes short and shallow.
A slow, longer exhale brings you back down.
copy.instagram_caption:
Jaw tight, shoulders up, vaguely wired mid-scroll? This 30-second reset fits before you carry on.

Take your eyes off the screen and do two physiological sighs: inhale through your nose, add a short top-up sip, then exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 to 8 seconds.

Then take one slow 4-6 breath (in for 4, out for 6), or three if you have time. Keep it gentle, and stop if you feel dizzy.

copy.facebook_message:
Mid-scroll is often when you notice it: jaw set, shoulders up, breath shallow. That's a good moment for a 30-second reset.

Take your eyes off the screen and do two physiological sighs: inhale through your nose, add a short top-up sip, then exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 to 8 seconds. Follow with one slow 4-6 breath (in for 4, out for 6), or three if you have time.

Slow breathing near 6 breaths a minute has the strongest research support. The effect is modest. It can help you feel calmer, but it won't switch stress off. Stop if you feel dizzy.

Our full guide has five calming patterns as 60-second scripts, each with a free timer.
